questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.1 Identify safe practices for picking up a load
questions.text: Before picking up a load, what should the operator verify?

answers.text: The load is within rated capacity, balanced, secure, and suitable for the forklift
The load looks heavy enough to improve traction
The operator can lift first and check capacity later
The load can be carried on fork tips if the route is short

explanations.a: Safe load pickup begins by verifying capacity, balance, security, and suitability before lifting. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Stability-related check: load weight must stay within capacity and should not be guessed.
explanations.c: Answer boundary: capacity must be checked before lifting.
explanations.d: Shutdown-control review: tip loading can damage the forklift and create instability.

questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.1 Identify safe practices for picking up a load
questions.text: How should forks be positioned before lifting a palletized load?

answers.text: Inserted only under the front edge of the pallet
Properly spaced and driven as far under the load as practical
Kept above the pallet while the mast tilts forward
Narrowed together at one edge of the pallet

explanations.a: Travel-surface note: using only the fork tips increases instability and damage risk.
explanations.b: Proper fork position helps support the load and keep the load close to the forklift. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Elevated-load clue: forks must support the load before lifting.
explanations.d: Fork-clearance note: poor fork spacing can make the load unstable.

questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.1 Identify safe practices for picking up a load
questions.text: During forklift operation training, What should an operator do before backing away with a picked-up load?

answers.text: Raise the load high before backing so others can see it
Back immediately because the load is now secure
Check behind and on both sides for pedestrians or other traffic
Sound the horn once and ignore blind spots

explanations.a: Visibility check: raised loads can reduce stability and visibility.
explanations.b: Parking-procedure review: a secure load does not remove backing hazards.
explanations.c: The workbook directs operators to check behind and on both sides before backing up. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Fork-position note: horn use helps, but operators still need to check the area.

questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.1 Identify safe practices for picking up a load
questions.text: Which action supports safe load pickup?

answers.text: Travel with the load raised at eye level
Tilt the load forward while reversing away
Lift the load while the forklift is still moving quickly
Slightly tilt the load back and lower it to travel height after backing clear

explanations.a: Practical safety note: raised travel reduces stability and may block visibility.
explanations.b: Hazard-recognition review: forward tilt can make the load less stable.
explanations.c: Backing-safety clue: lifting should be controlled and not combined with unsafe movement.
explanations.d: Tilting back and lowering the load helps stabilize it before travel. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.1 Identify safe practices for picking up a load
questions.text: Why should operators be cautious with fork extensions?

answers.text: Extensions can protrude from the backside of the load and change handling characteristics
Extensions remove the need to drive under the load
Extensions make pedestrian checks unnecessary
Extensions always increase forklift capacity

explanations.a: The workbook warns operators to be cautious with extensions because they can protrude from the back of a load. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Material-handling note: proper positioning remains important.
explanations.c: Safe-use logic: pedestrian checks remain required before backing or moving.
explanations.d: Travel-surface note: extensions can reduce capacity and change load center.

questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.2 Identify safe practices for traveling with a load
questions.text: During forklift operation training, What speed should be used when traveling with a load?

answers.text: A safe operating speed that allows the forklift to stop safely
The fastest speed that avoids immediate collision
A speed chosen only by production demand
A speed that requires sudden braking at corners

explanations.a: The workbook states forklifts should be operated at a speed that permits safe stopping. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Stacking-safety note: speed must allow safe stopping and control, not just avoid instant collision.
explanations.c: Visibility check: production pressure does not override safe operation.
explanations.d: Parking-procedure review: sudden braking can affect load control and stability.

questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.2 Identify safe practices for traveling with a load
questions.text: Which action should operators avoid while traveling?

answers.text: Keeping safe spacing from other forklifts
Sudden braking, sharp turns, horseplay, and stunts
Sounding the horn near blind areas
Following plant speed limits

explanations.a: Horn-use clue: safe following distance reduces collision risk.
explanations.b: The workbook warns operators to avoid sudden braking, turn in sweeping motions, and never engage in horseplay or stunts. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Practical safety note: horn use near blind spots helps warn others.
explanations.d: Hazard-recognition review: following traffic regulations supports safe operation.

questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.2 Identify safe practices for traveling with a load
questions.text: How should an operator cross railroad tracks?

answers.text: Without checking the surface condition
Parallel to the tracks at high speed
Diagonally when crossing is necessary and safe to do so
With the load raised high

explanations.a: Answer boundary: surface conditions remain important for safe travel.
explanations.b: Shutdown-control review: parallel travel can destabilize the forklift or trap wheels.
explanations.c: The workbook states operators should cross railroad tracks diagonally. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Material-handling note: raised loads increase instability.

questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.2 Identify safe practices for traveling with a load
questions.text: Which statement best addresses traveling with a load? What is the recommended load position during travel?

answers.text: Raised high to improve forward clearance
Tilted forward to increase speed
Dragged along the floor to prevent tip-over
Slightly above grade and slightly tilted back

explanations.a: Elevated-load clue: high loads reduce stability and may block visibility.
explanations.b: Fork-clearance note: forward tilt can destabilize the load.
explanations.c: Load-pickup clue: dragging loads can damage material and equipment and create hazards.

questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.2 Identify safe practices for traveling with a load
questions.text: How should operators drive when carrying a load that obstructs forward view?

answers.text: Drive in reverse when appropriate and maintain visibility in the direction of travel
Raise the load higher to see underneath it
Lean outside the operator compartment while driving forward
Drive forward anyway and hope pedestrians move

explanations.a: The workbook notes that if the load obstructs forward view, driving in reverse is usually recommended. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Fork-position note: raising the load reduces stability.
explanations.c: Capacity-control review: leaning out can expose the operator to crush and struck-by hazards.
explanations.d: Horn-use clue: operators need adequate visibility and pedestrian protection.

questions.objective: 5.3 Identify safe practices for placing and stacking loads
questions.text: Which load requires additional caution during placing and stacking?

answers.text: An unusually shaped or off-center load
A balanced load within capacity on sound pallets
A load already stacked square and straight
An empty pallet handled at a controlled speed

explanations.a: The workbook specifically instructs operators to use additional caution with unusually shaped or off-center loads. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Stability-related check: a balanced sound load is less unusual but still needs normal safe handling.
explanations.c: Answer boundary: a properly stacked load reflects safe placement.

questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.3 Identify safe practices for placing and stacking loads
questions.text: Which statement best addresses placing and stacking loads? Before raising a load for placement, what should the operator do?

answers.text: Keep moving so the load reaches the rack faster
Completely stop the forklift
Raise the load before checking for pedestrians
Raise the load while turning into position

explanations.a: Travel-surface note: movement while raising increases collision and stability risks.
explanations.b: The workbook instructs operators to completely stop before raising a load. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Elevated-load clue: pedestrians must not be exposed to elevated-load hazards.
explanations.d: Fork-clearance note: raising while turning can reduce stability.

questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.3 Identify safe practices for placing and stacking loads
questions.text: Who may pass under an elevated portion of a forklift?

answers.text: Solely if the elevated forks are empty
Solely trained workers wearing hard hats
No one, whether the forklift is loaded or empty
Solely the spotter during stacking

explanations.a: Visibility check: empty elevated forks still create a hazard.
explanations.b: Parking-procedure review: hard hats do not make standing under elevated forks safe.
explanations.c: The workbook states that no one may walk, stand, or pass under the elevated portion of a truck, whether loaded or empty. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Fork-position note: a spotter should not stand under elevated portions.

questions.name: Safe Operation: Loads, Travel, and Shutdown
questions.objective: 5.3 Identify safe practices for placing and stacking loads
questions.text: What should the operator do when stacking a load?

answers.text: Stack off-center if the load is light
Tilt forward before the load is over the rack or stack
Use speed to push the load into position
Stack it square and straight while using controlled movements

explanations.a: Practical safety note: off-center stacking can cause load shift or collapse.
explanations.b: Hazard-recognition review: forward tilt before placement can destabilize the load.
explanations.c: Backing-safety clue: pushing or striking can damage loads and create hazards.
explanations.d: The workbook instructs operators to stack loads square and straight. This is the correct answer.

questions.text: During training, an operator is handling a load in the workplace. Before backing out after placing a pallet, what should be verified?

The rack can be bumped lightly to free the forks

The operator can turn while forks remain inside the pallet

explanations.c: Safe-use logic: loads should be stacked square, straight, and stable.
